post.description:
Correct the RUT of a ficha (ADR-0087 §1), an operation of its own: `update` keeps the RUT immutable. The RUT travels in the body, never a URL, and is stored canonical (módulo 11), as `register` stores it. **`expectedUpdatedAt` is required**: a ficha that changed since your read is a **409 `stale_write`**. A RUT another live ficha of this practice holds is a **409 `rut_already_registered`**. **A RUT the ficha already has answers `200` with the ficha and writes nothing but its audit line**, so a retry of a correction that landed is not a 409. `reason` is required, from a closed catalogue.

Every correction is recorded in the identity history (`listPatientIdentityChanges`) with the value before and after, sealed, who made it with the roles they held, when and why; and the patient is told by e-mail that the identification of her ficha was corrected — the date, the time and the clinic, **never what and never who** (one notice waits at a time; none without an e-mail on file). Answers the ficha as `get` answers it to the caller. **A doctor or a receptionist corrects it**; an administrator is refused at the guard (403). A ficha that is not this practice’s is the guard’s 404, audited by the guard; a deleted one is this operation’s 404. Audited: a correction, a repeated one as `correct_rut:unchanged`, and each refusal this operation decides — a deleted ficha’s 404 and the two 409s — as a denial; a malformed id and a body the validation refuses leave none. The RUT is stored without leading zeros, which its check digit cannot see: `033333333-3` is `33333333-3`, the same RUT.

patch.description:
Partially update the ficha (the RUT is not here: `correctPatientRut` corrects it). Every change is audited; null clears a nullable field, and so does listing it in `clearFields` (0.77.0) for a client whose encoder omits a `nil`. **Send `expectedUpdatedAt`** — the `updatedAt` you read. Without it the write is last-write-wins: two clinicians correcting the same field silently overwrite each other and the first correction is lost with no error anywhere. With it, a ficha that moved since your read is refused with **409 `stale_write`**; re-read and re-apply your change on top. The server never merges — a clinical correction is not something to reconcile automatically.

**A change of the contact is announced** (`ADR-0057` §5, 0.63.0) — the e-mail, the phone, the address, the postal code or the coordinates —, in the same transaction: each professional with an upcoming appointment with the patient, other than you, reads what changed in `listMyContactChangeNotices`, and she is told by e-mail that her contact data changed — when and where, never who or what; when her e-mail changes, the address she had is told as well. One notice to her waits at a time: a change made while one is waiting adds nothing to it. Sending the value already on file announces nothing (the write itself still happens, and moves `updatedAt`). Coordinates are kept with six decimals, rounded half away from zero, and the notice says them as kept. A contact that changes from somewhere else under your write, again and again, is also a 409 `stale_write`: re-read and send the change again. Until 0.63.0 a lost update answered `conflict`; it answers the `stale_write` documented here.

**A change of the identification is recorded** (`ADR-0087`, 0.92.0) — a name, the birth date or the registered sex —, in the same transaction: the identity history (`listPatientIdentityChanges`) keeps the value before and after, sealed, who made it with the roles they held, and when; and she is told by e-mail that the identification of her ficha was corrected — when and where, never what or who, one notice waiting at a time, none without an e-mail on file. The social name and the gender are what she declares, not an identification, and record nothing. Sending the value already on file records nothing. An identification that changes from somewhere else under your write, again and again, is also a 409 `stale_write`.

post.description:
Write a clinical note for a patient (doctor only), optionally linked to the appointment it documents. All six sections travel inside ONE encrypted envelope (§7.6).

**Since payload v4 the note follows the Chilean printed form**, in this order: motivo de consulta (`chiefComplaint`), anamnesis, examen físico (`physicalExam`), hipótesis diagnóstica (`diagnosticHypothesis`), indicaciones (`instructions`), observaciones adicionales (`additionalObservations`). Only `anamnesis` is required.

**`chiefComplaint` is NOT the appointment’s `reason`.** That one is what the patient typed when booking; this one is what the professional records as the real reason for the visit. They differ routinely — a patient books the wrong specialty and the visit becomes a referral — and both are kept. This is the one the printed record states.

**`diagnosticHypothesis` is prose, not codes.** The coded diagnoses are `recordDiagnosis` rows against the CIE-10 catalogue; this is the free-text judgement the form asks for.

**A note naming an appointment whose record is CLOSED is refused with 409 `record_sealed`** — after the seal the way to correct the record is `writeAddendum` on an existing note, never a second note. An appointment closes when its treating professional calls `closeAppointment`, or when the platform’s closure window runs out after it ends, whichever comes first — the window is `recordWindows.closureHours` on `GET /v1/me` and the deadline of one appointment is its `closureWindowEndsAt`. No client hard-codes the number.

**The seal only reaches notes that NAME an appointment.** `appointmentId` is optional by design (an evolution can exist outside a booked slot, e.g. a phone follow-up), and a note sent without one names no act, so no closure governs it and this route keeps accepting it.

**Coded diagnoses can travel with the note** (`diagnoses`, 0.97.0), in its transaction: one write, so one unknown code is a 422 `unprocessable` and nothing lands.

**A retry with the same `clientId` is answered before the appointment is judged** (0.98.1): a note written before its record was sealed answers 201 with the stored note on its retry, never `record_sealed`, so do not rewrite it as an addendum. Two sends of one key at the same instant leave one note, and both are answered with it.

post.description:
Book an appointment. Overlapping the professional’s active agenda is a `409 professional_busy` (until 0.127.0 the generic `conflict`), which you can confirm as an overbook (below).

**Who asked decides whether it is born confirmed** (ADR-0057, 0.61.0). `requestedBy: PATIENT` — she asked, by phone or in person — books it `CONFIRMED`, confirmed by the practice; left out or `PRACTICE`, the practice proposes it and it waits `SCHEDULED` until she confirms it. A DOCTOR books an hour she asked for only on their own agenda, since booking it confirms it (403 otherwise); a proposal stays open to any member. A home visit that is confirmed keeps the patient's address as it was then (`homeVisitAddress`).

**Closed time is a `409` you can confirm** (ADR-0086 §6, 0.95.0): an hour inside an absence of the professional, on a holiday they did not open, or inside the break they keep after an appointment answers `closed_time_absence`, `closed_time_holiday` or `closed_time_break`; the same request with that kind in `confirmClosedTime` books it.

**A taken hour is a `409` you can confirm too** (ADR-0100, 0.127.0): the same request with `overbook` — its reason, and a doctor's optional note — books it over the hour the professional holds, as an overbook (`overbookReason` on every read). Who may is who may book. The platform caps them per professional and day (`overbook_limit_reached`). A key you used for another booking is still `conflict`.

post.description:
Drive the appointment lifecycle (ADR-0013): SCHEDULED → CONFIRMED → COMPLETED | NO_SHOW, and a `REQUESTED` appointment → CONFIRMED, which is how the practice ACCEPTS a request. An illegal move is a 409. **Who may: STAFF and ADMIN for any appointment of the practice, DOCTOR for their own only** — a doctor moving a colleague's appointment is a 403.

**Accepting a request confirms it** (ADR-0057, 0.61.0, **breaking**): an acceptance sent as `SCHEDULED` is a 409, and nothing moves into `SCHEDULED` any more. Confirming records how (`confirmedBy`): `PRACTICE` for an hour the patient asked for, `PRACTICE_FOR_PATIENT` — confirmed for her, by phone — for one the practice proposed. A home visit confirmed keeps her address as it was then (`homeVisitAddress`). **A sealed record is never confirmed** (409), though it is still corrected to its outcome.

**This operation no longer cancels** (`ADR-0055`, 0.56.0, breaking). Ending an appointment is an act of its own: `cancelAppointment` for a booked hour, `declineAppointmentRequest` for a request. `status: CANCELLED` is refused with 400 `cancel_operation_required`.

A retry with `clientId` answers 200 with the move ALREADY made; without `clientId` a move to the status the appointment already has is a 409.

**A request to MOVE an hour** (`ADR-0054`) is a `REQUESTED` appointment whose `rescheduledFromId` names the hour she wants to leave; the agenda shows it too. **Accepting it (`CONFIRMED`) also cancels that old hour**, in the same transaction, as the practice acting on her request (`cancellationReason: PATIENT_REQUEST`), and she is told the hour moved. It is a 409 when the old hour no longer stands — cancelled, attended or sealed meanwhile — because accepting would give her two hours or bring back a finished one: decline it instead.

post.description:
Move an appointment to a new time, and optionally a new place, in ONE operation (`ADR-0054`, 0.55.0). The old hour is cancelled as the practice's act — `cancellationReason` required, `cancellationNote` optional, exactly as `cancelAppointment` cancels — and the new one is booked in the same transaction, for the same patient and the SAME professional, with `rescheduledFromId` pointing at the old one. Returns the NEW appointment.

**Who may:** the same as cancelling — STAFF and ADMIN for any appointment of the practice, a DOCTOR for their own (403 otherwise). Only a `SCHEDULED` or `CONFIRMED` appointment moves: a request, a cancelled or finished one is a 409, and so is a SEALED record. The new hour meets every refusal `book` meets: 404 for a patient whose ficha was deleted or for an unknown place, 409 for a retired place — **including the old hour's own place when you name none**, since nothing new is booked where the practice no longer attends — `professional_busy` for the professional's overlap, and `patient_unavailable` when the patient is busy at that hour. If she had asked to move this same hour and the practice had not answered yet, that request is withdrawn, for the `cancellationReason` you give here.

**`clientId` is required.** A retry answers 200 with the move that already happened — also when it arrives while the first attempt is still running. One key names one write: a key you already used for a booking or for another move is a 409, and `book` answers a key used for a move with a 409 as well. The patient is told with a service notice that names both hours and the clinic, and nothing else.

**The new hour on closed time is a `409` you can confirm**, as in `book` (ADR-0086 §6, 0.95.0): the hour being left and her request to move it are not neighbours for the break.

**The new hour over a taken one is a `409 professional_busy` you can confirm with `overbook`**, as in `book` (ADR-0100, 0.127.0). The hour being left does not count against the day's limit, since this move cancels it; an overbook moved to a free hour lands as an ordinary one.

post.description:
Seal the record of this act: after it, the clinical note of this appointment can no longer be written and a correction is an addendum. **`COMPLETED` says the appointment happened; `closedAt` says its record is sealed** — two axes, and this moves the second one.

**Only the treating professional may close**, and a colleague gets a 403: they can read what is still open, but sealing is the clinician asserting that what they wrote is what happened. Staff and admin cannot close at all.

**Irreversible, and idempotent for free:** there is no re-open operation, and closing an already-closed appointment answers 200 with the `closedAt` it already had — never a 409, so a retry needs no `clientId`. If the closure sweep got there first you will see its seal, with `closedBy` null.

**When the sweep becomes due is published per row**, as `closureWindowEndsAt`, and it is non-null exactly while the record is open **and the sweep will actually reach it** — draw the countdown from it rather than adding the window to `endsAt` yourself. The window itself is platform configuration and arrives as `recordWindows.closureHours` on `GET /v1/me`; no client hard-codes either number.

**A REQUESTED appointment is never swept** (`ADR-0045` enmendada). A request is a patient asking: until the practice answers, no act was agreed and there is no record of one to seal. Its `closureWindowEndsAt` is therefore `null` — draw no countdown on it — and the practice keeps being able to DECLINE it, which is what frees the slot and the patient's one pending request with that professional.

**What the seal reaches (`ADR-0049`):** the record of this attention, not one edge of it. Sealed once closed, each answering **409 `record_sealed`** — a new clinical note or receta naming this appointment, a new exam order, a new diagnosis or vital on one of its notes, a new attachment, and the invalidation of a diagnosis or a vital. No retry ever succeeds, by anyone: after the seal the only correction path is `writeAddendum`, within its own window.

**And exactly what it does NOT reach, so you never have to infer it:** a clinical note written without an `appointmentId` names no act, so no closure governs it or its children — `appointmentId` is optional by design (an evolution can exist outside a booked slot). An exam RESULT hangs off the order, not off this appointment, so a lab answering days later is never refused. Completing an upload begun before the seal is not refused either — the bytes are already stored and only STARTING a new attachment is governed. And a receta can still be annulled: issuance is sealed, annulment is the only valve a mistaken prescription has.

The member is always present in both cases.

delete.description: Remove a block. A real delete: it is a current fact about the week, not the record of an act. **409 when live appointments sit inside it**, and the body lists them in `blockingAppointments` (id, start, status) so the screen can name them without a second call. The body carries no patient: to move them, `listBlockingAppointments` returns the same list with each one’s patient. Blocking means FUTURE and in REQUESTED, SCHEDULED or CONFIRMED; CANCELLED, NO_SHOW and COMPLETED never block. Move or cancel them first: `rescheduleAppointment` moves one in a single operation (`ADR-0054`) — it cancels the old hour and books the new one, linked — and a REQUESTED one is declined. Audited, and a refusal is audited as a denial. There is no force flag: the escape hatch would be an escape from the very rule this operation exists to enforce.

get.description: The settings of this professional’s whole agenda, as «Mi horario de atención» draws them (ADR-0086 §2, §3): `breakMinutes`, the break kept after every appointment, and `slotMinutes`, the length of a consultation where every weekly block agrees on one — `null` when they differ or there is none. A professional the practice does not hold — another practice’s, or nobody’s — is 404, and so is one who left the practice: an agenda nobody can run has nothing to configure.

patch.description: Set the break, the length of a consultation, or both, for this professional’s whole agenda (ADR-0086 §2, §3). At least one of `breakMinutes` and `slotMinutes`, or the request is a 400; only what is sent moves, and both in one transaction. **The length is set on every weekly block, at every place**, guarded by `expectedSlotMinutes`, the length the screen showed (`0` when it showed none), which is required with it: when the blocks no longer have it the request is a **409 `stale_write`** and nothing moves. A length some block is shorter than is a **400 `agenda_slot_too_long`** that names those blocks, and with no weekly block to set it on it is a **422**; in every refusal nothing moves, the break sent with the length included. Neither the break nor the length moves or refuses an appointment already booked: they change what is offered from now on — `getAvailability`, and the patient’s directory, booking and move. The practice’s own `book` and `rescheduleAppointment` do not read the break yet (ADR-0086 §6). An agenda write: a doctor sets their own, a receptionist those of the professionals assigned to her; an administrator is refused at the guard (403), and a profile that is not the caller’s is 404, the same as another practice’s. Audited: a change, and each refusal this operation decides — the 404 of a profile outside the caller’s agendas or one who left the practice, the 409, the 400 `agenda_slot_too_long` and the 422 — leaves one line whose `action` says what was asked, e.g. `agenda_settings:break:5:slot:30`. post.description: Open extra hours (ADR-0086 §4): a dated window of hours the weekly blocks do not have, at one place, with its own length — the mirror of an absence, which closes. Local wall clock on a calendar day of the practice’s zone: a window that starts after now (a day before today, or today at an hour already passed, is a 400), on a day at most 365 days ahead (a 400 otherwise), so that no new opening can meet one already over. Its slots join the weekly ones in `getAvailability`, the patient’s directory, booking and move, where the place is one she can book at, as for a weekly block; the break and the booked appointments apply as to any slot, and an absence over it closes it. **It opens its own hours on a holiday**, closed or answered «Sin atención» alike. It never overlaps a weekly block of that place on that weekday, nor another live opening of that place and date: a **409 `working_hours_overlap`**. The place must be an ACTIVE place of this practice. Never rewritten: cancel it and open another. An agenda write: a doctor opens their own, a receptionist those of the professionals assigned to her; an administrator is refused at the guard (403), and a profile or a place that is not the caller’s is 404. Audited: an opening, and each refusal this operation decides — the 404 of a profile outside the caller’s agendas or of a place, the 400 of a window out of range and the 409 — leaves one line `declare_extra_hours`. What is refused before it is not that line: a profile the practice does not hold is the guard’s 404 and a 403 the guard’s 403, each with the guard’s own line; a malformed id, a body the validation refuses and a slot longer than the window, decided from the body alone, leave none.

Free slots for one professional at one of their places. **A slot carries a start and an end and nothing else** — this is not the clinic’s agenda with fields removed, and that emptiness is the security property: there is no field here to leak.

It takes the two opaque ids a search returned and resolves the clinic server-side, so the tenant never appears in a request or a response. A professional who opted out is a **404**, indistinguishable from one who never existed. A range wider than 62 days is refused rather than truncated, because a truncated agenda looks exactly like a full one. **A national holiday’s weekly hours are absent from the result unless the professional opened it** (since 0.89.0, ADR-0086 §1: a holiday nobody answered is closed to them, and `listHolidays` names it), **but extra hours the professional declared on it are offered** (since 0.91.0, ADR-0086 §4: their slots join the weekly ones on any day), so a holiday with slots is open, whatever `listHolidays` says. The hours inside a declared absence are absent too (0.51.0). **Slots step the slot plus the professional’s break**, and a slot within the break of a booked appointment is absent too (since 0.90.0, ADR-0086 §2).

**Being away is not a 404 any more (0.73.0, ADR-0062).** Until then a professional who was away vanished from the directory and from this route; now they stay findable, their hours inside the absence are simply not offered, and `listDirectoryClosedPeriods` says when they are away.

Each profile also carries how that clinic says it can be reached (`practiceContact`, `ADR-0058`, 0.66.0): the health centre is the support you contact, and the field is null until the clinic publishes a phone or an e-mail, and while the platform has the clinic suspended.

Correct your e-mail, phone or address at ONE clinic. These four are the whole editable surface: a name or a date of birth is how that clinic knows whose record this is, and is refused by the database, not merely omitted from this schema.

**Every change is announced** (`ADR-0057` §5, 0.63.0), in the same transaction: the clinic's professionals with an upcoming appointment with you are told what changed, inside their app, and you are told by e-mail that your contact data changed — when and where, not what. When the e-mail itself changes, the address you had is told as well. One notice waits at a time: a correction made while one is waiting adds nothing to it. Sending the values you already have announces nothing, and a phone that reads as one is kept as the practice keeps it (`+56 9 1234 5678` is `+56912345678`). A 409 `stale_write` means your contact changed at the same time from somewhere else, more than once: read your profiles again and send the correction again.

**To clear a field, send it as `null` or list its name in `clearFields`** (0.77.0): the second is for a client whose encoder omits a property it holds as `nil`, so it could never say `null`. Both mean the same.

post.description:
Book a slot the professional published, using the opaque ids the directory returned. The slot is re-verified server-side against the same availability computation you read, so a time that is not actually free is a 409. You must already be enrolled at that clinic.

**Read `status` on the response.** A professional may take bookings instantly (`SCHEDULED`) or by review (`REQUESTED`) — and may set that differently for someone they have already attended than for a new patient. A `REQUESTED` appointment already HOLDS its slot, so it cannot be given away while the practice decides; declining it is what frees the time. You may hold only one pending request per professional at a time (409).

**Send `clientId`** (0.70.0): a retry answers 201 with the appointment you already made, not a 409 «that hour is taken» for the hour you have just booked. It is the key `rescheduleMyAppointment` already takes, and one key names one write.

post.description:
Cancel one of your own appointments. An appointment already completed, marked no-show or cancelled by the practice or the platform is a 409.

**An appointment YOU already cancelled answers 204 again, since 0.76.0** (task `0062`): a retry after a lost answer is the end you asked for, and it is not judged against the free-cancellation window either. Nothing is written, the practice is not told a second time, and the card keeps the first reason. One the practice or the platform cancelled stays a 409, because that is news: the card says whose cancellation it was.

**A 409 also means the record of that attention is SEALED.** (The one sealed record that answers 204 is an hour YOU cancelled: the closure sweep seals cancelled hours too, and a retry is still the end you asked for.) Once it is closed — by the professional or by the closure sweep — nobody can cancel it any more, the practice included, so do not tell the patient to phone in for this one. Note that a swept appointment can still read SCHEDULED on the card: the seal and the status are different axes.

A professional may set a free-cancellation window; past it this returns `cancellation_window_closed` and the practice must do it. The window is on your appointment card as `cancelCutoffHours` (since 0.102.0 — before it, this sentence promised a field the card did not have), so the app can say so BEFORE the patient tries.

**The body is required since 0.52.0** (`ADR-0052`): `cancellationReason`, from the patient's own list. There is no free text, by design. The card then shows the cancellation as hers — `cancelledBy: PATIENT` — and the practice sees the same reason.

**Only a booked appointment is cancelled** (`SCHEDULED` or `CONFIRMED`) since 0.56.0 (`ADR-0055`, breaking): a `REQUESTED` one is a 409 here — withdraw it with `withdrawMyAppointmentRequest`, which refuses a request the practice has just accepted instead of cancelling the hour it became.

post.description:
Confirm an appointment the practice proposed to you (`ADR-0057`, 0.61.0): one in `SCHEDULED` with `requestedBy: PRACTICE`, whose hour is still ahead and whose record is open. Returns its card, now `CONFIRMED` with `confirmedBy: PATIENT`. It takes no body.

**The side that was asked confirms**, and nobody else has to. **One already `CONFIRMED` answers 200 with its card, whoever confirmed it**: that is the end you asked for. Any other is a 409 `conflict`: one you asked for that the practice has not confirmed yet — a booking or a request of yours, `requestedBy: PATIENT` —, one made before 0.61.0 that says nobody asked (`requestedBy: null`), and one cancelled, attended, missed, sealed or whose hour has begun. **Nobody is notified**: the practice sees the confirmation in its agenda.

Confirming means you checked the data the practice holds for you (`listMyPatientProfiles`); correct it first with `updateMyPatientProfile`. **For a home visit the practice keeps your address as it is at the moment you confirm**: a correction you make later reaches only the appointments confirmed after it.

post.description:
Withdraw one of your REQUESTS (`REQUESTED`) — a request for a new appointment or a request to move one (`ADR-0055`, 0.56.0). `cancellationReason` from your own list is required; there is no free text. No free-cancellation window applies: nothing was agreed yet. **Nobody is notified**: the practice sees it in its agenda, as it saw the request.

**409 `request_already_answered` when the practice accepted it first:** it is a booked appointment now, and nothing changes. Re-read your appointments; to give that hour up, cancel it (`cancelMyAppointment`), within its window. For a request to move an hour, the acceptance already moved it. A request already withdrawn, declined or expired answers 204: that is the end you asked for.

post.description:
Move one of your appointments to another slot of the SAME professional (`ADR-0054`, 0.55.0), named the way `bookMyAppointment` names one. Returns the NEW appointment, whose `rescheduledFromId` points at the old one.

**Read `status` on the response**, as when booking. `SCHEDULED`: the professional takes bookings instantly, the move is done, and the old appointment reads `CANCELLED` as yours, with your `rescheduleReason`. `REQUESTED`: the practice reviews bookings, so NOTHING was cancelled — your old hour stands until the practice accepts, and if it declines you keep it and are told so (unless the old hour began, was attended or was sealed meanwhile: then there is no hour left to keep, and the decline reads as an ordinary cancellation of the one you asked for). A pending request counts as your one pending request with that professional (409 `pending_request_exists`), and it is withdrawn if the old hour is cancelled or moved another way first. If nobody answers it within the platform's request window it expires (`ADR-0056`): it reads `CANCELLED` with `cancelledBy: PLATFORM`, your old hour stays as it was, and you are told. Withdrawing it yourself is `withdrawMyAppointmentRequest`, and tells nobody.

Only a `SCHEDULED` or `CONFIRMED` appointment moves (409 otherwise), and only inside the professional's free-cancellation window (`cancellation_window_closed`), because moving it cancels it. The new slot passes every check a booking passes.

The new appointment keeps the old one's channel.

**`clientId` is required.** A retry answers 200 with the move you already made, also while the first attempt is still running.

post.description: Issue a single-use enrolment code for a patient you have identified IN PERSON. The code is returned once, lives 15 minutes and is never stored in readable form — reissue rather than look it up. Issuing does not invalidate a previous unredeemed code.

get.description:
Your contact-change notices, newest first (`ADR-0057` §5, 0.63.0). One notice per change of a patient's e-mail, phone, address, postal code or coordinates, made while you held an upcoming appointment with her — a request, a booked hour or a confirmed one that had not begun. Made from either side: by a member of this practice, or by the patient from her own app. **You are never told of a change you made yourself.** Each notice says who (the patient), when, and each field with its value before and after; never who made the change. A notice is one-way: there is nothing to answer. It stays until you mark it read (`markMyContactChangeNoticeRead`), and then for the retention the author sets; read ones are still listed, with `readAt`.

A patient under a restriction of processing is absent from this list, as her hours are from the agenda, and so is a patient whose ficha was retired. Audited. Default 50 per page, clamped server-side to 100 — an out-of-range `limit` is corrected, never an error. Keep requesting with the returned `nextCursor` until it is `null`. An unreadable `cursor` is a 404 rather than a silent first page.

Nothing marks a notice unread. A notice that is not yours — unknown, another practice's, or a colleague's — is a 404.

get.description:
The changes of your contact at ONE clinic, newest first by `changedAt` (`ADR-0057` §6, 0.65.0): your e-mail, phone, address, postal code or coordinates, whoever made the change — the clinic's staff or you. **Only the changes made since your account was linked to this clinic's ficha** (the link in force): what came before is not yours to read, whether it happened before you were linked, while your link was cut, or while another account held the ficha. Each says when it was made and each field with its value before and after; never who made it. That is what you need to recognise a change, or not. `disownedAt` says whether you already marked it. The values are read in the app, never sent by e-mail.

A clinic you have no link at is a 404, as it is for a change that is not yours. Default 50 per page, clamped server-side to 100 — an out-of-range `limit` is corrected, never an error. Keep requesting with the returned `nextCursor` until it is `null`. A `cursor` that is not one is a 404 rather than a silent first page.

post.description:
Mark one change of your contact «No reconozco este cambio» (`ADR-0057` §6, 0.65.0). **It tells the clinic and it is recorded:** the mark appears in the list the clinic's doctors, staff and admins share (`listContactChangeDisowns`), with the values before and after, and stays there — among the open ones, then among the closed once one of them closes it. While your record is under a restriction of processing the mark is stored and answered as usual, but that list leaves your record out. **It reverts nothing by itself** — the clinic corrects your record as it always does, and can cut your access if that is what is needed. Marking a change again is the same 204 and writes nothing. A change that is not yours — unknown, another patient's, another clinic's, or from before your link to this clinic's ficha — is a 404.

**This covers a change you did not make yourself and the clinic did, or made by mistake; it does not cover someone else using your account.** Whoever holds your account can read this route too. If you cannot enter your account, contact your health centre: that path does not depend on the account.

get.description:
The changes of a patient's contact that she marked «No reconozco este cambio» (`ADR-0057` §6, 0.65.0), the open ones first and the newest mark first (by `disownedAt`) in each group. **One list for the whole practice**: any doctor, staff member or admin sees the same marks. Each says which patient, when the change was made and when she marked it, each field with its value before and after, and whether a member closed it and who. **A mark reverts nothing:** correct the ficha with `update` as always, and close the mark with `resolveContactChangeDisown` to leave record that it was attended.

A patient under a restriction of processing is absent from this list, as her hours are from the agenda, and so is a patient whose ficha was retired. Audited. Default 50 per page, clamped server-side to 100 — an out-of-range `limit` is corrected, never an error. Keep requesting with the returned `nextCursor` until it is `null`; a mark closed while you page may show again among the closed ones, and none is lost. A `cursor` that is not one is a 404 rather than a silent first page; one that names no mark of this practice answers an empty last page.

post.description: Close a mark: leave record that a member attended it (`ADR-0057` §6). The platform stamps `resolvedAt` and keeps the identity of the FIRST member who closed it; closing it again changes nothing and answers 204 as well. Nothing reopens a mark. It does not touch the ficha. A mark the list leaves out (a patient under a restriction of processing, a retired ficha) can still be closed by its id. A mark that is not this practice's — unknown, or another practice's — is a 404, audited as a denied attempt.

get.description: The contact history of a ficha (since 0.118.0, task 0129): each change of the e-mail, the phone, the address, the postal code or the coordinates, newest first, a page at a time. Each says the fields with their values before and after, when, and who: a member of this practice (their id and their profile's name) or the patient from her own app. A change made before 0.118.0 says when and what, and `changedBy.kind: null`. `disownedAt` is her «No reconozco». A patient under a restriction of processing reads as an empty page, as in the inbox and the marks. Read by whoever reads the ficha's identity, a doctor or a receptionist. A ficha the practice does not hold, a deleted one and a `cursor` that is not a change of this ficha are a 404, audited as a denial. Audited as a read of the patient. Default 50 per page, clamped to 100.

get.description:
What patients did with the hours of the agendas you run, from their own app, newest first (`ADR-0099`, 0.126.0). A doctor reads the notices about their own hours; a receptionist, those about the professionals assigned to her (`ADR-0066`), including acts from before the assignment. One notice per act, of four kinds: she cancelled a booked hour, asked for an hour, asked to move one, or moved one at once (`kind`). **What the practice does is never announced here**, and neither is a request she withdraws (`withdrawMyAppointmentRequest`) or a proposed hour she confirms (`confirmMyAppointment`), nor a booking a practice that takes bookings at once received: it is in the agenda.

Each notice says what, who (the patient), which hour and when; **never her reason**, which stays on the appointment. Read and unread are yours alone: a colleague who marks one read does not mark it for you. `unreadCount` is the number for the menu.

A patient under a restriction of processing is absent from this list and from the count, as her hours are from the agenda, and so is a patient whose ficha was retired. Audited. Default 50 per page, clamped server-side to 100 — an out-of-range `limit` is corrected, never an error. Keep requesting with the returned `nextCursor` until it is `null`. An unreadable `cursor` is a 404 rather than a silent first page.

Nothing marks a notice unread. A notice you cannot see — unknown, another practice's, or about an agenda you do not run — is a 404.

post.description:

Until the first call the limit is 2 a day, the number the author set to start with.

get.description: The channels this patient objects to receiving messages about her appointments by (`ADR-0061`, 0.72.0): one entry per channel with an opposition in force, who filed it and when, and an empty list when she objects to none. **Read it before you cancel or move one of her hours:** the notice that says so does not reach her by a channel she objects to, and the practice should reach her another way. It says nothing of the notices inside the apps, which do not leave the system. It is not a consent, and revoking a consent does not file one.

post.description: File, for a patient and on her word, an opposition to receiving messages about her appointments by one channel (`ADR-0061`, 0.72.0; Ley 21.719). **Staff or admin.** From then on the outbox cancels every message to HER about her appointments by that channel — reminders and notices alike — with the code `channel_opted_out`, and each cancellation is audited. Not affected: the notices to the professional, the notices inside the apps, and the notice that her contact data changed, which is a security notice and always goes. It is not rectification or erasure: her contact data is untouched. One opposition is in force per channel: filing it again answers `200` with the one in force, whoever filed it, and writes nothing. It is available while she is under a restriction of processing, since it narrows what is processed. A patient who is not this practice's, or whose ficha was retired, is a 404, audited as a denied attempt.

With none in force it answers `204` as well: that is the end you asked for. **An opposition the patient filed herself is a `409` `conflict`:** only she withdraws it, from her own app, so that the practice cannot turn the messages back on against what she asked for. A channel the contract does not name, and a patient who is not this practice's, are 404.

get.description:
Who acted on which record, newest first, over the last 90 days. Cursor-paginated; default 20 per page, clamped to 100. **Identifiers only, never content**: no name, RUT, diagnosis or note title appears here. Resolve `resourceId` against the roster you already hold and render a generic entry when it is absent — that means the record is outside what you may see, which is correct. `action` and `resourceType` are plain strings on purpose: a value outside the documented catalogue must cost one odd entry, never the whole page. Chat and transport never appear.

**This feed is no longer successes only — branch on `outcome`.** Exactly one denial is published: `resourceType: "patient_portal"` with `action: "portal_access.enrol"` and `outcome: "deny"`, which means somebody tried to claim a ficha **that already has an owner**. Rendering it as something that happened is worse than not showing it. The clinic is the only party who can answer it — revoke the account, reissue the code, telephone the patient — which is why it comes here rather than to the platform trail (`ADR-0033` amended).

**Nothing about a patient under a restriction of processing appears** (Ley 21.719): not an access to her ficha, not one to any record of hers, and the page is filled from what remains. That somebody opened her ficha is information about her. The denial above is the exception, because it protects her record, which a restriction does not stop. The audit trail itself still holds everything.

The patients who read it are the ones you attended, by the rule `RETURNING_ONLY` uses (a COMPLETED appointment with you, through a link to a live ficha), whatever your `visibility`: being found and giving your contact are separate decisions, so a `HIDDEN` professional can still give it. They read it with `listMyProfessionalContacts`. **Turning a switch off hides it from the app at once, and nothing more**: a patient who already copied it keeps it.

A switch on with no value behind it is a 400. Answers the stored setting, the phone canonical (E.164). **Only the professional, on their own profile** (`ADR-0088`): a receptionist or an administrator is a 403, and a colleague's profile, or a retired one, is a 404 — as it is for an id that names nothing. Each write is audited. The 403 and the 404 of a profile that is not yours are audited as denials; a malformed id or body is refused before anything is read, and writes no line.

info.title: lumemed-cloud API
info.description: Backend contract for the Lume Cloud medical platform. Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json. A string's `minLength` and `maxLength` count UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript counts them: a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, such as most emoji, counts two, and an emoji built from several characters (a flag, a skin tone) counts each of them. Count the same way before sending, or a text within a limit counted another way is refused with 400.

tags.name: sandbox

tags.name: reference
tags.description: The reference catalogues (ADR-0042): the CIE-10 diagnosis vocabulary (DEIS/MINSAL) and the territorial codes of Chile (SUBDERE). Public data of the state, served to both client tiers, read-only — loaded by migrations, never by a request. `listReferenceReleases` names the edition being served.

tags.name: prescriptions
tags.description: Recetas (ADR-0019, ADR-0047). **What this API stores is CONTENT, never a legally issued prescription**: the document with legal standing is the one the app PRINTS, signed and stamped by hand. No electronic signature, no SNRE. Doctor only; immutable — a mistake is annulled and a new one issued, and the database's UPDATE grant reaches exactly `annulled_at`.

tags.name: contact-change-notices
tags.description: Every change of a patient's contact data is announced (ADR-0057 §5): each professional with an upcoming appointment with her, other than the member who made it, reads what changed here, inside the app. Never by e-mail, never in a push. And the patient's answer to a change (§6): she marks it «No reconozco», and the practice — its doctors, staff and admins, one shared list — reads the marks and closes them.

tags.name: record-windows
tags.description: The two windows of the clinical record (ADR-0048) — how long a record stays open for writing after the act ends, and how long its author may append after the seal. Platform configuration, OWNER-only write: moving either number costs a deploy of this backend and nothing on the iPad. The values in force are published on `GET /v1/me`; the deadline of one record is published on the record.

clientId.description: Retry key you generate: a fresh value per composed note, reused across retries of that same note. **Send it on every write.** Without it, a retry — a timeout, a double tap — writes a SECOND note for the same act, and no clinical table allows deletion: the copy can only be annulled. With it, a retry answers 201 with the note already stored, and writes none of its `diagnoses` again. **The stored note wins over the retry's body:** a retry that changed the text, the appointment or the codes is still answered with what the first attempt stored, so an edited note is a NEW key. Honoured since 0.97.0: before it, this route accepted the key and ignored it.

diagnoses.description: Coded CIE-10 diagnoses written in the SAME transaction as the note (since 0.97.0): the note and its codes land together or not at all, so a failure between two calls can no longer leave a note without the codes it was written with. At most 20, and **at most one with `isPrimary: true`** — a second primary is a 400. Each code must be in the catalogue `searchCie10` serves, or the whole write is a 422 `unprocessable` and nothing lands. A missing `description` is recorded as the catalogue's own wording. The note's `clientId` covers its codes too: a replay answers with the note already stored and writes no code again. The response is the note; read the codes with `listNoteDiagnoses`. `recordDiagnosis` stays for adding or correcting a code on a note already written.

addendumWindowEndsAt.description: When this note stops accepting addenda, or `null` when no clock is running. With no `appointmentId`, `null` means it never will: the seal does not reach the note. With one, `null` means the clock has not started, and it starts when the attention is sealed; an instant is the last moment an addendum lands, inclusive, and one sent after it is a 409. It never moves when the platform changes the addendum window, unlike `AppointmentDto.closureWindowEndsAt`. An ISO 8601 instant in UTC, always with three fractional digits and a trailing `Z`, as in `2026-09-28T21:35:25.250Z`.

requestedBy.description: Which side asked for this hour (ADR-0057, 0.61.0). `PATIENT`: she asked — by phone, in person — so the practice, which was asked, confirms it by booking it: the appointment is born `CONFIRMED`, with `confirmedBy: PRACTICE`. A DOCTOR does so only on their own agenda, as with `transition`: on a colleague's it is a 403. `PRACTICE`, the default: the practice proposes the hour, and it stays `SCHEDULED` until she confirms it from LumeMedLink, or the practice confirms it for her by phone (`transition` to `CONFIRMED`, recorded as `PRACTICE_FOR_PATIENT`). A replay of the same `clientId` answers with the appointment as it was booked, whatever this field says.

confirmClosedTime.description: The kinds of closed time of the professional you confirm this hour may fall on (ADR-0086 §6, 0.95.0): `ABSENCE` (inside an absence), `HOLIDAY` (a holiday they did not open, with no extra hours covering it), `BREAK` (inside the break they keep after an appointment). **Left out, an hour on closed time is a `409`** whose `type` names the first kind it falls on (`closed_time_absence`, `closed_time_holiday`, `closed_time_break`); re-send the same request with that kind here to book it. Name only what you were told: a kind you did not confirm is refused again, even if it appeared since. Nothing opens to patients, and the audit trail records the hour as placed on closed time, and on which.

overbook.description: Book this hour over one the professional already holds, as an OVERBOOK (ADR-0100, 0.127.0). **Left out, a taken hour is a `409 professional_busy`**; re-send the same request with this to book it. The hour is an overbook only if it is still taken when it lands: sent for a free hour, it books an ordinary one and `overbookReason` reads `null`. An overbook is never over the PATIENT's own commitments (`patient_unavailable` stays), it meets closed time as any hour (the hour it overlaps is not its break), and the professional may hold only as many on one day as the platform allows: past it, `409 overbook_limit_reached`. Audited as an overbook.

reason.description: Why the practice takes this hour over a taken one, from a closed list that is not clinical: `URGENCY`, `UNPOSTPONABLE_FOLLOW_UP` (a follow-up that cannot wait), `PATIENT_REQUEST`, `OTHER`.

note.description: The practice's own words about the overbook, stored exactly as sent and encrypted at rest, as a cancellation's note: **written by a doctor only** (a receptionist who sends it gets `403`), read by a doctor only, never by the patient. At most 500 UTF-16 code units: an emoji counts two or more.

clientId.description: Your own key for THIS booking, so a retry does not create a second appointment. **Send it**: a duplicate cannot be deleted — no clinical table grants DELETE — so the extra appointment is cancelled and stays in the agenda for ever. Unique only to you within this patient, and for as long as the appointment exists: the key is stored with it and never forgotten. So generate a fresh random key (a UUID) for each new booking and resend it only on that booking's retries — a counter that starts again with each session answers a new booking with an old appointment, and books nothing. Replaying it returns the appointment you already created, not a 409. One key names one write: a key you already used for a MOVE is a 409 here. To move an hour, use `rescheduleAppointment` (ADR-0054), never a cancel and a new booking — that sends the patient two notices that read as two unrelated events.

requestExpiresAt.description: When this request becomes due to expire if nobody answers it: the platform's request window after it was made (ADR-0056). `null` for anything that is not an open `REQUESTED` row; a sealed one never expires. The platform ends it with a sweep, so it may stay open a while after this instant. Draw any countdown from this instant, never from a number of hours. Once ended it reads `CANCELLED`, with `cancelledBy: PLATFORM` and `cancellationReason: REQUEST_EXPIRED`.

requestedBy.description: Open vocabulary — new values may appear; treat an unknown one as opaque, never as an error. Known values: PATIENT, PRACTICE. Which side asked for this appointment (ADR-0057, 0.61.0): `PATIENT` — she asked, from LumeMedLink or by phone or in person — or `PRACTICE`, which proposed the hour to her. **The other side confirms it.** While it waits, the appointment reads `REQUESTED` or `SCHEDULED`: a `SCHEDULED` one asked for by the practice waits for her (she confirms from LumeMedLink, or the practice for her by phone, `transition` to `CONFIRMED`), and one asked for by her waits for the practice. An appointment can also end — cancelled, attended or missed — without ever being confirmed. `null` on an appointment made before 0.61.0: not recorded, never «nobody».

confirmedBy.description: Open vocabulary — new values may appear; treat an unknown one as opaque, never as an error. Known values: PATIENT, PRACTICE, PRACTICE_FOR_PATIENT. How it was confirmed (ADR-0057, 0.61.0): `PATIENT`, by her from LumeMedLink; `PRACTICE`, by the practice as the side that was asked — booking an hour she asked for, confirming one she booked, or accepting her request — and also on an appointment made before 0.61.0, where nobody on record asked; `PRACTICE_FOR_PATIENT`, by the practice on her behalf, by phone, for an hour it proposed. It never changes once set. `null` while it is not confirmed, on one that ended without a confirmation, and on one confirmed before 0.61.0: not recorded.

homeVisitAddress.description: The address this home visit was confirmed for (ADR-0057 §2, 0.61.0): the patient's street, number, unit, commune and region as her record held them when it was confirmed, copied by the platform and never changed afterwards — a later correction of her address reaches only the appointments confirmed after it, not this one. A part her record lacked is `null`, and it carries no coordinates. `null` on any other channel, on a home visit not yet confirmed, and on one confirmed before 0.61.0.

requestExpiresAt.description: When your request becomes due to expire if the practice does not answer it: the platform's request window after you made it (ADR-0056). `null` for anything that is not an open `REQUESTED` card. The platform ends it with a sweep, so it may stay open a while after this instant; once ended it reads `CANCELLED`, with `cancelledBy: PLATFORM`. A request to move an hour that expires does not touch the old hour: it stays as it was.

requestedBy.description: Open vocabulary — new values may appear; treat an unknown one as opaque, never as an error. Known values: PATIENT, PRACTICE. Which side asked for this appointment (ADR-0057, 0.61.0): `PATIENT`, you — from here, or by phone or in person — or `PRACTICE`, which proposed the hour to you. **The other side confirms it.** A `SCHEDULED` card with `requestedBy: PRACTICE` waits for you: confirm it with `confirmMyAppointment` (or the practice confirms it for you, by phone). One you asked for waits for the practice. `null` on an appointment made before 0.61.0: not recorded.

confirmedBy.description: Open vocabulary — new values may appear; treat an unknown one as opaque, never as an error. Known values: PATIENT, PRACTICE, PRACTICE_FOR_PATIENT. confirmedAt.description: When it was confirmed, stamped by the platform. Set exactly when `confirmedBy` is, and `null` otherwise. An ISO 8601 instant in UTC, always with three fractional digits and a trailing `Z`, as in `2026-09-28T21:35:25.250Z`.

startsAt.description: When the slot begins, exactly as `getDirectoryAvailability` returned it. An ISO 8601 instant in UTC ending in `Z`, as in `2026-09-28T13:00:00Z`; seconds and their fractions are optional, and an offset, even `+00:00`, is a 400.

endsAt.description: When the slot ends, exactly as `getDirectoryAvailability` returned it. An ISO 8601 instant in UTC ending in `Z`, as in `2026-09-28T13:00:00Z`; seconds and their fractions are optional, and an offset, even `+00:00`, is a 400.

clientId.description: Your own key for THIS booking, so that a retry never makes a second appointment. **Send it**: a connection that drops after the write leaves you not knowing whether the hour is yours, and the same booking sent again would otherwise be refused as «that hour is taken» — by the hour you have just booked. Replaying it answers 201 with the appointment you already made, as it stands now, also while the first attempt is still running; it is not a 409, and it does not check the slot again, so it answers even when the practice stopped taking bookings since. The key is yours within the clinic of the professional, and it lives as long as the appointment does: generate a fresh random key (a UUID) for each new booking and resend it only on that booking's retries — a counter that starts again with each session answers a new booking with an old appointment, and books nothing. One key names one write: a key you already used to move an hour (`rescheduleMyAppointment`) is a 409 here. Without it a booking is as it was, and a retry of it is not recognised.

cancellationReason.description: Why you withdraw it, from your own list. The practice sees it in its agenda; nobody is notified.

endsAt.description: When the new slot ends, exactly as `getDirectoryAvailability` returned it; it must be after `startsAt`, or the request is a 400. kind.description: Open vocabulary — new values may appear; treat an unknown one as opaque, never as an error. Known values: CANCELLED, REQUESTED, MOVE_REQUESTED, MOVED. What the patient did, from her own app. `CANCELLED`: she cancelled a booked hour (`appointmentId`). `REQUESTED`: she asked for an hour and it waits for the practice (`appointmentId`, `REQUESTED`). `MOVE_REQUESTED`: she asked to move an hour; `appointmentId` is the request, `previousAppointmentId` the hour it would leave, which stands until the practice accepts. `MOVED`: she moved an hour at once; `appointmentId` is the new hour, `previousAppointmentId` the one she left, now cancelled as hers.

patientId.description: The patient who did it. Her ficha, her name included, is `GET …/patients/{id}`.

appointmentId.description: The hour the act is about, as the agenda holds it: open it to read the reason she gave, behind the same access as any appointment. It may have changed since — a request accepted or declined, an hour cancelled by the practice.

previousAppointmentId.description: The hour a move leaves (`MOVE_REQUESTED`, `MOVED`); null for any other kind.

occurredAt.description: When she did it, by the platform's clock. An ISO 8601 instant in UTC, always with three fractional digits and a trailing `Z`, as in `2026-09-28T21:35:25.250Z`.

unreadCount.description: How many of ALL your notices you have not read, not only this page's, under the same filter as the list: the number for the menu. A request with `limit=1` reads it without bringing the inbox.

dailyLimit.description: How many overbooks a professional may hold on one day of the agenda's wall clock, counting the live ones (not cancelled). `0` allows none.

Known values: PRACTICE, PATIENT. `PATIENT` when she filed it herself; `PRACTICE` when the clinic filed it for her, on her word. It decides who withdraws it: she withdraws any opposition of hers, and the practice withdraws only what the practice filed.

registeredAt.description: When it was filed, by the platform's clock. An ISO 8601 instant in UTC, always with three fractional digits and a trailing `Z`, as in `2026-09-28T21:35:25.250Z`.
